item.title: Undertone 1.18.15
item.description:
Task chats learn from you. When you're working on a task in Ask and tell it something new, like "this is a DM to Mike", Undertone saves that to memory and rewords the task to match. A small "Task updated" note shows what changed.

Drafts look right. Copy-ready messages now show bold, italics, code and links instead of raw * and <url|title> markup. Copy keeps that formatting when you paste into Slack, Mail or Docs.

"Say more" is now "Elaborate".

Undertone 1.18.14

Undertone Pro is coming. Profile & Settings › General has a new Undertone Pro section: what Pro adds (automatic briefings, research ahead, unlimited meeting prep, study guides, org chart import and private AI credits) and a place for your license key. Every Pro feature stays free for everyone during the beta, and your meetings never leave your Mac either way: a license key holds only your email and when it ends, and it's checked on your Mac.

Undertone 1.18.13

A calmer Home. Your week now sits in one quiet line beside the greeting. Below it are two columns: what's next and your tasks on the left, the latest recap, answer coaching and words to learn on the right. Cards and colored tags gave way to simple sections, task details read as one plain line, and Start and "I know this" appear when you hover. Ask is a slim command bar that lights up when you type.

Undertone 1.18.12

Faster answers about people. Questions like "who reports to Will?" are now answered from your imported org chart right away, in a few seconds, instead of searching your connected sources first.

Undertone 1.18.11

A roomier Home. Cards now stack in columns by height, so a long list no longer leaves empty space beside shorter cards, and the latest recap fills in wherever there's room. Up next rows take only the height they need, and on wide screens Home uses more of the window.

Undertone 1.18.8

Terms ready when you open them. During a call, each new term is looked up in your sources in the background, one at a time, so clicking it shows the people, links and context right away. Looking one up by hand is faster too. Turn it off in Settings › Hints if you like.

One recap per meeting. When Undertone updates or quits mid-call, the meeting carries on and gets a single recap at the end, instead of one at every restart.

Fewer answer cards in presentations. No cards for a presenter's own questions, or for "what is X?" when X is already explained.

Do more with an answer. Under every Ask answer: Say more, copy it as text or as an image, and thumbs up or down. A thumbs down asks what was wrong, can try again, and shapes your next answers.

A minimized panel that's yours. Drag it anywhere on screen. It's now Tide, a small disc whose water rises while people talk and whose rim turns blue when a question is for you. Five more styles are in Settings › Minimized panel: Waterline, Edge tab, Ticker, Halo and Surface.

Undertone 1.18.4

No more "You" lines when you didn't speak. If your speakers play into your Mac's microphone (or you're muted in the call app, which doesn't turn off the Mac's mic), those lines are now recognised as the call's audio and left out, including in meetings you already saved.

Who's talking, best guess. When someone hands over by name ("John, take it away"), the lines that follow are marked with that name and a question mark. Unsure lines stay blank.

Fewer pointless answer cards. No cards for small talk, or when someone else is handed the floor for their update. A slightly misheard version of your name still counts as you, and recaps add things asked of everyone to your tasks.
